 Denzel Washington is one of the most legendary American actors of all time. The two-time Academy Award winner landed his first Oscar in 1990 for his role as Private Silas Trip in Glory (1989) and again in 2002 for his turn as a corrupt police officer in the nail-biting crime thriller Training Day (2001). His decorated time on the big screen is yet to show any signs of slowing, with the actor — now in his 70s — continuing to pick up varied roles in the industry.

 Washington is set to star in a new, currently untitled thriller helmed by Amazon MGM Studios and United Artists, and opposite an MCU favorite to boot, per Deadline . Actress Teyonah Parris has made two on-screen MCU appearances as Monica Rambeau. Making her Marvel debut in the TV series WandaVision in 2021, she played a S.W.O.R.D. agent enlisted to investigate the strange behavior of Wanda (Elizabeth Olsen) while posing as a neighbor. She went on to reprise that role alongside Brie Larson in The Marvels (2023). And while the actress has expressed an interest in joining the MCU again, it's unclear if that will play out.
 In the upcoming film, Washington will portray a former police detective serving a life sentence in prison. Having been diagnosed with terminal brain cancer and told that he only has six months to live, he is granted compassionate leave. As he returns home, the detective reunites with his estranged daughter, played by Parris. He also meets a grandson he never knew he had. As Deadline writes: "He only wants to make amends and forget his dark past, but his dark past has not forgotten him."

 Notwithstanding her MCU stint, Parris has been building an incredible resume, getting her start in Dear White People (2014) , Chi-Raq (2015), and If Beale Street Could Talk (2018). She then went on to star in They Cloned Tyrone (2023) alongside John Boyega, Matchbox (2026) with John Cena, and the upcoming Apple TV's upcoming sports movie Running with Rhea Seehorn. Spike Lee's Chi-Raq was one of Amazon Studios’ first theatrical feature releases, so the new role arguably brings the actress full circle after a hugely successful decade.

 The thriller will be directed by Christopher McQuarrie and executive produced by Tim Honigman and Joe Guest. It is one of McQuarrie's higher‑profile projects not centered on Tom Cruise, with the director having overseen a string of Mission: Impossible movies as well as Jack Reacher, also starring Cruise, back in 2012.
 Some sources suggest that Washington was able to squeeze the upcoming Amazon thriller into his schedule after Netflix halted its historical epic about the ancient North African statesman Hannibal Barca. Production reportedly stopped so that the studio could iron out some budget issues. Whether that project will still go ahead remains to be seen.
 The untitled thriller will open in theaters on October 1, 2027.
